_note: Killer-query presets (team/briefs/pm-2026-11-24-killer-queries-a4.md; population rule: product/decisions.md D8). Source file: scripts/presets.py reads it at build time, measures the real fill of each preset's keys over the preset's in-scope population in the published index, and writes docs/api/v1/presets.json (what the app and agents read). Never hand-edit fill numbers; there are none here. filters use the app's own URL keys f_<field>_(min|max|value). gate keys = filter keys + require; every gate key and column must be carried in the index (facet or column field). min_fill defaults to 0.8, min_brands to 2. scope (D8): sources = source tiers a row must carry at least one of (default ["manufacturer"]); include_discontinued (default false); by = filter keys that define the population (a row a known value rules out on one of them leaves the denominator of every other key; unknown always stays in; a key is never scoped by itself); rows whose status for a key is not_applicable leave that key's denominator. basis = the sentence the card shows.

pdo_pill.label: Samsung 45 W
pdo_pill.rule: yes when an output port lists a PPS range covering 9 to 11 V at 4.5 A or more; no when every output port lists its PPS (or the product states no PPS) and none qualifies; otherwise unknown

presets.title: Laptops with upgradable RAM, 32 GB+ possible, 14 inch, under 1.4 kg

scope.basis: Current US-market laptop configurations with a maker spec page (Lenovo PSREF, ASUS).

presets.title: USB-C monitors 27 inch and up with no PWM flicker and 65 W+ power delivery

scope.basis: Current monitors with a maker spec page. Rows known to have no USB-C input do not count against the power-delivery fill. ENERGY STAR and DisplayHDR listing-only rows are out of scope: those lists never carry PWM or USB-C power.

presets.title: 2 TB NVMe SSDs with a real DRAM cache (not HMB, not DRAM-less)

scope.basis: SSDs with a maker spec page. Drives known to be SATA do not count against the DRAM fill. NAND type is shown but not filtered: makers rarely print it (see D8).

presets.title: Power banks with PPS and a 45 W+ port (open one for the Samsung 45 W check)

scope.basis: Power banks with a maker store page. Banks known to top out below 45 W do not count against the PPS fill: they cannot do Samsung 45 W either way.

Current monitors with a maker spec page. 1440p means a native resolution ending in x1440 (2560x1440, 3440x1440, 5120x1440). The refresh filter is the native rate, not an overclock ("165Hz OC" counts as 144). ENERGY STAR and DisplayHDR listing-only rows are out of scope. PWM and USB-C power are shown as columns, not filtered.

presets.title: Robot vacuums that fit under 3.5 in (89 mm)

scope.basis: Current robot vacuums with a maker spec page. Height is the robot body as the maker states it; a raised LiDAR turret counts when the maker includes it. Mop lift and self-empty are shown as columns, unknown kept visible, not filtered.

presets.title: LiFePO4 power stations with 1 kWh or more

scope.basis: Current power stations with a maker spec page. Stations known to hold under 1 kWh do not count against the chemistry fill. UPS switchover time is not shown yet: the key is in the profile but not carried in the index.

presets.title: Surge protectors listed to UL 1449 with 2,000 J+ and a VPR of 400 V or less

scope.basis: Current US power strips and surge protectors with a maker spec page. UL 1449 is the surge standard; UL 1363 alone is a plain power strip. VPR is the highest voltage protection rating the maker lists across line, neutral and ground.

presets.title: What panel does each TV size use?

scope.basis: Current TV models with a maker spec page. ENERGY STAR listing-only rows have no size class, so they can never sit on the size grid.

presets.title: TVs with a 120 Hz panel and at least one 4K 120 Hz HDMI input (port count shown)
presets._id_note: The id predates the retitle (2026-11-25, product/demand-r6.md): kept stable so old ?preset= links work. The title says what the gate checks today (any 4K 120 Hz port). next_gate is not applied: switch to it when hdmi.ports_4k120 reaches the fill gate in this scope (72% on 2026-11-25), then the title becomes "4 HDMI inputs at 4K 120 Hz".

next_gate.when: hdmi.ports_4k120 fill >= min_fill in this preset's scope

scope.basis: Current TV models with a maker spec page and a native 120 Hz (or faster) panel. TVs known to have a 60 Hz panel do not count against the 4K 120 Hz fill: they cannot show 4K at 120 Hz. A TV qualifies when its maker states that at least one HDMI input takes 4K at 120 Hz; the number of such ports is shown as a column where the maker lists them per port (LG often states only that its inputs support 4K 120 Hz).

presets.title: Wi-Fi 7 routers with a 6 GHz band, ranked by 5 GHz link rate (stream counts shown where the maker states them)

scope.basis: Routers, mesh systems and access points with a maker spec page. Wi-Fi 5 and Wi-Fi 6 models do not count against the 6 GHz fill. Per-band stream counts are not filtered: TP-Link and NETGEAR never print them (see D8).

presets.title: Purifiers with a smoke CADR of 260+ cfm (enough for about 400 sq ft)

scope.basis: Purifiers on the ENERGY STAR list or with a maker page. The CADR is ENERGY STAR-certified (AHAM AC-1 test) on most rows; each value's basis is on its detail page. 260 cfm comes from the AHAM room-size rule (room area = 1.55 x smoke CADR, so 400 sq ft needs 258 cfm). Ranking per filter dollar is not offered: filter prices are preview-only by policy (dated store prices).

presets.title: Full-size counter-depth refrigerators up to 36 in wide with 20+ cu ft, ENERGY STAR, 600 kWh/yr or less

scope.basis: Full-size (not compact) refrigerators their ENERGY STAR filing declares counter-depth, by concrete model number. ENERGY STAR certified patterns (one filing covering several finishes or hinges, e.g. BRB106003**) are left out: their width does not transfer to a specific SKU (A1 ruling). Capacity is the DOE total volume (fresh + freezer), never the larger adjusted volume or a model-number size class. Counter-depth is the maker's own ENERGY STAR declaration; ENERGY STAR publishes no depth, so check the depth on the maker's sheet.

presets.title: 24 in dishwashers with 14+ place settings using 3.5 gal or less per cycle (energy use shown)

scope.basis: Standard-size dishwashers whose unit width fits a 24 in cutout (23 to 24.25 in as filed with ENERGY STAR; 23.5-23.9 in is typical), by concrete model number. ENERGY STAR certified patterns are left out: their width does not transfer to a specific SKU (A1 ruling). Water and energy are DOE normal-cycle figures (Appendix C1). Noise is shown when a maker states it, but is not part of the gate: only one maker publishes dBA we can read, so a noise filter would cover one brand.
